_comment: Specialization phases: one per Python career pathway not covered by the core phases. transform.py inserts them after p17. Item ids are positional (sN.sK.M): append new lines, never reorder or delete.

phases.name: Data analysis & visualization
phases.aim: Load, clean, analyse and chart tabular data, and report conclusions that hold up.

res.w: The pandas author's book, free to read online
Indexing, groupby, reshaping, time series
Short exercises in the browser
Figures, axes and the object-oriented API
Statistical plots on top of Matplotlib

items: NumPy arrays, dtypes, broadcasting and vectorized operations.
pandas Series and DataFrame: indexing with loc and iloc, and why chained assignment fails.
Reading CSV, Excel, JSON and SQL; setting dtypes and parsing dates on load.
Cleaning: missing values, duplicates, inconsistent categories, outliers.
groupby, aggregation, pivot tables, melt and merge.
Time series: resampling, rolling windows, time zones.
Descriptive statistics, distributions, correlation vs causation.
Hypothesis tests and confidence intervals with SciPy, and when they apply.
Charts with Matplotlib and seaborn: choosing the chart for the question.
Notebooks for exploration, scripts for anything you run twice.
Pick a public dataset and write down the question before opening it.
Clean it in a script that runs end to end from the raw file.
Answer the question with at least three charts, each with a one-line takeaway.
State the limitations: sample, bias, missing data.
Publish the report as a static page or PDF generated by the script.

gate.note: Use a dataset you have not seen before.
items: Clean a messy dataset without looping over rows.
Explain the difference between a merge that multiplies rows and one that does not.
Pick the right chart for a comparison, a trend and a distribution, and justify each.
Explain why a correlation in your data does not prove causation.

A single-purpose tool someone else uses, such as a file renamer or a log viewer.

Settings persist between runs in the correct per-user folder.
Keyboard shortcuts and a usable tab order.
An installer or bundle that runs on a machine without Python.
Tests for the logic layer that run without a display.

Show your logic tested without starting the GUI.
Install and run your app from its bundle on a clean machine.
Explain where your app stores user data on Windows, macOS and Linux.

Correct exit codes, tested.

Show a solver's error shrinking as you refine the step or sample count.
Rerun your whole analysis from a clean environment and get the same figures.

phases.name: Quantitative finance
phases.aim: Analyse market data, build backtests without bias, and measure risk correctly.

res.w: Quantitative economics and finance in Python
Date ranges, resampling, rolling statistics
Exact decimal arithmetic for money
Mean-variance and other portfolio optimization

items: Prices vs returns: simple and log returns, and adjusting for splits and dividends.
Money with Decimal, and where float is acceptable.
Resampling and aligning time series across markets and time zones.
Backtesting: lookahead bias, survivorship bias, fees and slippage.
Risk metrics: volatility, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, value at risk.
Portfolio construction: diversification and mean-variance optimization.
Train/test splits over time, walk-forward testing, and why random splits leak.
Market data APIs, rate limits and storing data for reproducible research.
The difference between research code and execution code.
Simulate a simple strategy on daily data with fees and slippage.
Make lookahead impossible by construction, and test that it is.
Report returns, volatility, Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown.
Compare against a buy-and-hold benchmark.
Run a walk-forward test and report out-of-sample results separately.

gate.note: Paper trading only. Nothing in this phase uses real money.
items: Show a test that fails if your strategy reads a future price.
Explain how fees and slippage change your strategy's result.
Compute maximum drawdown by hand for a short series and match your code.
Explain why a strategy that works in-sample can fail out-of-sample.
